Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Subject: Access controls & support access - follow-up from today's demo

Hi Jordan / Sally -

Thanks again for your time today - great conversation. Quick recap and next steps on the access controls / support access items we discussed: 

Summary of requirements I captured
- RBAC & least-privilege: FinTrust needs role-based access with a clear admin/ops/reader separation and per-route restrictions for PII.
- Support access: engineers may need temporary elevated access for troubleshooting; you want an auditable break-glass process with approvals and post-incident review.
- Logging & retention: immutable audit logs for user actions + per-request token/log retention policy; legal has asked about retention timeframe for logs and PII.
- Data residency: production data must remain in the US region and options for VPC/private deployment were of interest.

Attachments: I've included a short summary of Redwood's access controls and a stub ACL template below for your team to review (redwood_access_controls_summary.pdf referenced).

Proposed next steps
1) Can you confirm the retention window you expect for PII and audit logs (e.g., 1 year vs 5 years)?
2) Please identify which internal teams will require support access (SRE, AppOps, Support) and which names to start in the ACL matrix.
3) I'll follow up with a technical deep-dive to walk through our break-glass flow and logging export options.

If this aligns, I'll send the ACL template and SOC2 summary for your security team.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa - thanks for the recap. A few clarifications from Security and Legal: 

- Retention: Legal is leaning toward a 5-year retention for audit logs that contain identifiers linked to PII; please confirm if Redwood supports configurable retention windows per-customer.
- Break-glass: we need details on the approval workflow and an audit trail that includes who approved, why, and the before/after actions taken by the elevated session.
- Support access: can you provide an ACL matrix we can populate with names and intended roles? We'd like to see recommended role definitions (example: reader, operator, admin) and the minimum privileges per role.
- SOC2 evidence: Security would like a trimmed SOC2 summary or relevant controls to accelerate our internal review.

Also copied our security mailbox for visibility. If you can share the ACL template and SOC2 summary, we'll start filling in the names and propose times for the tech deep-dive.

Jordan / team -

Per your ask, attaching two quick artifacts to accelerate the security review: ACL_matrix.xlsx (simple CSV-style template) and SOC2_summary.pdf (high-level control mapping). Below are concise answers to your questions: 

1) Configurable retention: Yes - Redwood supports per-customer configurable retention for audit logs and request traces. We can set immutable retention to 5 years for logs that contain PII identifiers; logs are stored in an immutable audit store (append-only) and can be exported to your S3 if you prefer.

2) RBAC & role definitions (recommended starter set)
- reader: view-only, cannot export PII or request token keys.
- operator: can run queries and view logs, cannot manage deployments or change routing.
- admin: full access to deployments, model routing, and RBAC management.
- support_elevated: temporary role used only during break-glass sessions.

3) Break-glass / support access flow
- Request: Engineer creates a time-limited elevation request in the Console with a justification.
- Approval: A designated approver (manager or on-call) approves via email/Console; approval records stored in the audit log.
- Session: Access is granted via a short-lived token (15-60 min) with session recording of all API calls.
- Post-incident: An automatic post-incident review is generated and notifications sent to the security mailbox.

4) Auditing & logging
- Every elevation and API call is logged with UID, caller, action, and request payload hash.
- Logs are write-once (WORM) with tamper-evidence and can be replicated to your S3/GCS.

5) Data residency
- We can pin your instance to US-East (primary) and offer VPC/private deployment for additional network isolation. Keys can be customer-managed (KMS/HSM).

Attachments: ACL_matrix.xlsx (template - please add names/teams/desired role), SOC2_summary.pdf (control mappings).

Next suggested steps
- Fill the ACL matrix with initial names (SRE/AppOps/Support) and return; we'll pre-populate role suggestions.
- Schedule a 45min technical deep-dive next week to walk the security team through the break-glass demo and log exports. I've included a HubSpot link for the deal and a Drive folder with the artifacts above.
